# Ezra Chapter 3 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 469r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/EZR_003_page_001.jpg

---

**3:1** And-when-arrived the-month the-seventh, and-the-sons of-Yisra'el [were] in-the-cities, the-people gathered-themselves [vaye'asfu] as-one-man [ke-ish echad] to Yerushalayim.

**3:2** And-rose-up Yeshua son of-Yotsadaq and-his-brothers the-priests [ha-kohanim], and-Zerubbavel son of-She'alti'el and-his-brothers, and-they-built the-altar [mizbe'ach] of-the-God of-Yisra'el, to-offer upon-it burnt-offerings [olot], as-written [ka-katuv] in-the-Torah [instruction] of-Mosheh the-man of-God.

**3:3** And-they-established the-altar upon its-bases [mekhonoteha], for-dread [be-eimah] was-upon-them from-the-peoples of-the-lands, and-they-offered upon-it burnt-offerings to-YHWH, burnt-offerings of-the-morning and-of-the-evening.

**3:4** And-they-kept [vaya'asu] the-feast of-Sukkot [booths] as-written, and-burnt-offerings day by-day [yom be-yom] by-number [be-mispar], according-to-the-ordinance [ke-mishpat], the-matter of-a-day in-its-day [devar yom be-yomo].

**3:5** And-after-this the-continual burnt-offering [olat ha-tamid], and-for-the-new-moons [chodashim] and-for-all the-appointed-times [mo'adei] of-YHWH the-consecrated-ones [ha-mequddashim], and-for-everyone freely-offering [mitnadev] a-freewill-offering [nedavah] to-YHWH.

**3:6** From-day one of-the-month the-seventh they-began to-offer burnt-offerings to-YHWH, but-the-temple [hekhal] of-YHWH had-not-been-founded [lo yussad].

**3:7** And-they-gave silver to-the-hewers [chotsvim] and-to-the-craftsmen [charashim], and-food and-drink and-oil to-the-Tsidonim [Sidonians] and-to-the-Tsorim [Tyrians] to-bring cedar-wood [atsei arazim] from the-Levanon [Lebanon] to-the-sea of-Yapho [Joppa], according-to-the-grant [ke-rishyon] of-Koresh king of-Paras upon-them.

**3:8** And-in-the-year the-second of-their-coming to-the-house of-the-God in-Yerushalayim, in-the-month the-second, began Zerubbavel son of-She'alti'el and-Yeshua son of-Yotsadaq and-the-rest of-their-brothers the-priests and-the-Levites, and-all the-ones-coming from-the-captivity [ha-shevi] to-Yerushalayim, and-they-appointed [vaya'amidu] the-Levites from-twenty years [ben esrim shanah] and-upward to-oversee [lenatse'ach] the-work of-the-house of-YHWH.

**3:9** And-stood Yeshua, his-sons and-his-brothers, Qadmi'el and-his-sons, sons of-Yehudah, as-one [ke-echad] to-oversee the-ones-doing the-work in-the-house of-the-God; the-sons of-Chenadad, their-sons and-their-brothers the-Levites.

**3:10** And-when-the-builders [ha-bonim] laid-the-foundation [yissdu] of-the-temple [hekhal] of-YHWH, they-stationed the-priests robed [melubashim] with-trumpets [chatsotsrot], and-the-Levites sons of-Asaph with-cymbals [metsiltayim], to-praise [lehallel] YHWH according-to-the-direction [al yadei] of-David king of-Yisra'el.

**3:11** And-they-responded [vaya'anu] in-praising [be-hallel] and-in-giving-thanks [be-hodot] to-YHWH, "For [he is] good [ki tov], for-forever [ki le-olam] his-covenant-faithfulness [chasdo] upon Yisra'el." And-all the-people shouted [heri'u] a-great shout [teru'ah gedolah] in-praising YHWH, because the-house of-YHWH was-being-founded [hussad].

**3:12** And-many from-the-priests and-the-Levites and-the-heads of-the-fathers [rashei ha-avot], the-old-men [ha-zqenim] who had-seen the-first house [ha-bayit ha-rishon] in-its-being-founded [be-yussdo], this house before-their-eyes, were-weeping [bokhim] with-a-great voice [qol gadol], and-many with-a-shout [bi-teru'ah] of-joy [simchah] to-raise [leharim] the-voice [qol].

**3:13** And-not the-people could-distinguish [makkirim] the-sound [qol] of-the-shout of-joy [teru'at ha-simchah] from-the-sound of-the-weeping [bekhi] of-the-people, for the-people shouted a-great shout [teru'ah gedolah], and-the-sound [ha-qol] was-heard to-a-distance [ad le-merachoq].

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.3 — "for dread was upon them":** The phrase *be-eimah alehem* is syntactically ambiguous. It may mean they established the altar *despite* their fear of the surrounding peoples, or *because of* their fear (seeking divine protection through sacrifice). The Masoretic cantillation supports the causal reading.

**v.11 — "For he is good, for forever his covenant-faithfulness":** This is the liturgical refrain *ki tov ki le-olam chasdo* found throughout the Psalms (Ps 136). Its use at the temple foundation connects this moment to Solomonic worship (2 Chr 5:13), establishing liturgical continuity.

**v.12-13 — The mixing of weeping and joy:** The verb *makkirim* ("distinguish") uses the hiphil of *nakar* — the people literally could not "cause-to-recognize" the difference between the two sounds. The text does not explain why the elders wept — whether from grief at the second temple's inferiority or from overwhelming emotion at the restoration.

*— EMET*
